messages:
sasha: Heads up: after canary rollout to us-east-1, I'm seeing rows from other orgs in the console runlist for a few users. Repro: go to /console/runs?workspace=foo and open run details. Screenshot incoming.

hal: Yikes. Which service owns the prefetch path? Any logs or request ids?

sasha: Got a sample trace and screenshot. Request id req_8a3f7c, user org=org-A but response contains rows with org-B. Paste of truncated log:

GET /api/console/runs?workspace=foo 200 req=req_8a3f7c user=alice org=org-A
prefetch: key=runlist:recent -> cache hit shard=3
queried-store: found 12 rows (orgs found=[org-A, org-B])

Looks like prefetch cache key omitted org scoping.

maria: Probable root cause. We added a small cache wrapper in PR #4216 to speed up runlist prefetch. If the key doesn't include org/workspace it will return a shared slice across tenants. Pinging @ji-hoon — your change touched that file.

ji-hoon: Yep that PR is mine. I used a short key to reduce key length: prefetchKey = "runlist:recent". Ugh — missed org. Quick fix: include org id and maybe user-tier. Example patch:

// old
prefetchKey := "runlist:recent"
// new
prefetchKey := fmt.Sprintf("runlist:recent:%s", orgID)

I'll open a hotfix branch now.

eng-oncall-bot: deploy: canary rollout started 2024-11-12T15:02:34Z -> services/console v2.9.1 (canary fraction=15%)

hal: Can we rollback the canary to stop any further bleed while the hotfix is prepared?

ben: I'd prefer rollback unless the hotfix is trivial and quick to verify. How long to get tests + deploy?

ji-hoon: Patch is tiny. Unit + integration run should be <10m. I'll push hotfix to canary and run a narrow verification set against affected users.

ops-bot: ops: applied hotfix to canary (deploy id=dep_998). Cleared prefetch cache for shards [1,2,3].

sasha: Confirming — rechecked 3 impacted users ~2m after hotfix, no cross-org rows. Will keep monitoring for 15m.

maria: I'll add a regression test that asserts the prefetch cache key includes org/workspace, and add an e2e assertion that every returned row.org == requester_org. Also filing follow-up to make cache wrapper require an explicit scope param.

ben: :thumbsup: Can we also add a telemetry alert for anomalous org-mix in responses? Simple rule: if any request returns rows with org != requester_org -> emit alert; if rate > threshold -> page.

hal: Agreed. Created ticket PLAT-7895 to add the alert + runbook + retrospective notes.

sasha: Thanks all. Leaving thread open for another hour then will close when clean.
